input_scope.input_tree_digest_algorithm: SHA256 over sorted relative path + NUL + each file SHA256 bytes

request_event_grain.description: One saved HTTP response observation for a GET or retained redirect hop; key=(aware retrieved_at normalized to UTC, response.url or requested_url).
request_event_grain.deduplication: Cached nested robots responses and repeated source references with the same key are counted once. Retained redirects are separate request hops, also deduplicated by this key.
request_event_grain.timestamp_meaning: For the current collector, retrieved_at is set at raw_get initialization before host lock/delay and requests.get; it is neither exact on-wire send time nor response completion time.
request_event_grain.response_observed_rule: An integer http_status and timestamp are present. A 503 is an observed HTTP response from the shared path, not proof of an origin-server response.
request_event_grain.phase_assignment: Company attempt-directory timestamp is compared with manifest worker8 paused_at; health preflight is separately labelled. HTTP observations from before retry start are analysed separately.
request_event_grain.requests_not_reconstructable: Robots responses on discarded intermediate redirect hops may be missing. Failed requests without saved status are separated below. Old initial captures generally lack redirect history. Counts are saved observations, not a complete packet/request log.
request_event_grain.role_overlap_note: Each event has a role set; no cross-role duplicate was observed in this retry.

retry.worker24_start_note: Manifest does not save a resumed_at time; first company event is the earliest retained proxy for restart.

mixed_period.warning: Mixed timestamps cannot establish the ordering of response completions.

actual_request_exceptions_without_saved_.cannot_infer_no_response_for_value_error: ValueError may occur while reading/parsing after response headers, which were not persisted.

prior_initial_outage.worker_count_evidence: No initial-run worker count in inspected manifest, response metadata or saved run JSON. before/README has a suggested resume command with workers8, not an initial execution log.
prior_initial_outage.post_onset_successes_note: Initial-run shared503 and successful bodies remained intermixed across hosts; the last retained successful initial observation is not evidence that all hosts were healthy until that time.
prior_initial_outage.comparability_limit: Initial response captures lack most redirect-hop history and an immutable collector version; observed-event densities are lower-bound proxies and cannot be compared as exact wire-request rates.

supported: Saved retry HTTP429 count is zero. Shared Invalid argument503 is distinct from the 15 TLS/connection-related503 responses.
All shared Invalid argument503 collector observations in the retry occur in the 24-worker segment; the 8-worker retry segment has none, but does have13 other upstream503 responses.
The worker increase and higher saved request-initialization density precede shared503 recurrence. This supports checking load/concurrency or aggregate quota as a hypothesis, without proving it.
The same215-byte body and SHA256 recur across six collector hosts and later JPX/Rakus healthchecks, supporting a shared outbound-path failure rather than issuer IR policy.

Followup single healthchecks remain faulty minutes after the last retained collector request initialization. This is compatible with persistent transport state or a cooldown/quota, not diagnostic of either.
Initial-outage shared503 also follows a dense saved burst, but its worker count and exact on-wire rate are unknown. Eight workers is not established as a safe threshold.
not_established: A documented or measured rate limit
Whether failure is aggregate quota, proxy resource exhaustion, tunnel state or origin/TLS behavior
That all other tools/network processes were idle
missing_measurements: Exact send, DNS/connect/TLS, first-byte and request-end times
Connection/stream reuse and active on-wire concurrency
Full response headers, Retry-After, rate-limit headers and transport trace IDs
Complete intermediate robots captures for redirects
Global outbound traffic from other processes/tools and backend quota metrics
interpretation.safe_followup_design: After confirmed recovery, use the same known-good URLs and fixed small batches, vary workers and global dispatch rate independently, retain UTC/JST send/end times and selected headers, and stop on cross-host shared failures. This analysis performs no such requests.
